sections.title: Blockers and prerequisites

paragraphs: 8 non-functional risk indicators were derived from the bytecode of the analyzed artifact: 4 high and 4 medium. They are structural indicators, not measurements; 3 of them need runtime validation before they are acted on.
Persistent classes shared across candidate domains (high, detected): affects 8 components in Owner Visit, Type Owner, Vet.
Entry points with no detectable security control (high, inferred): affects 6 components in Owner Visit, System Configuration, Vet.
No logging, metrics or tracing reference found (medium, inferred): affects 10 components in Application Clinic, Owner Visit, System Configuration and 2 more.
Repository query that returns a whole collection (medium, detected): affects 2 components in Type Owner, Vet.
Shared component used from two or more candidate domains (medium, detected): affects 1 component in Type Owner.
2 candidate domains (Application Clinic, System Configuration) hold technical concerns rather than a business capability; keep them as shared configuration or libraries, not services.

5 components (NamedEntity, PetType, BaseEntity, Person and 1 more) are used by two or more domains; decide on a library, a module or an owner before separating those domains, because a service would add a network call to every user.

6 libraries (Spring core and boot, Jakarta Persistence, Spring Web MVC and 3 more) already cross domain boundaries as ordinary dependencies; each extracted service includes them and none is a service candidate.

Not examined: configuration files and values; runtime behavior, load and failure handling; gateway, platform and network controls; source code of the shared components. A control that does not appear in the bytecode is not proven absent.
